summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and prior port infections was admitted for headaches, nausea, vomiting, and a supratherapeutic INR of 7.3. Initial concerns included intracranial bleed or infection, but brain MRI showed no acute findings. Her symptoms were attributed to a combination of factors: bacterial overgrowth from recent antibiotics, managed with metronidazole; aspiration pneumonia, diagnosed on chest X-ray and treated with levofloxacin; and a yeast vaginitis, treated with topical antifungals. Her INR normalized after holding warfarin, and she was restarted on her home dose. The pelvic MRI showed improvement in her prior pectineus abscess with no fluid collection. She responded well to treatment, with resolution of headaches, nausea, and fevers, and was discharged home on a 7-day course of oral antibiotics and antifungal therapy, with instructions to continue her home medications and follow up with her primary care provider.
